glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: edge-case | Severity: medium
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/companion.ts:16-26 (`freePort`)
- Finding: Classic TOCTOU port race: the port is bound, closed, and only then handed to the spawned Python process. Another process can grab it in between; the companion then fails to bind and the whole scenario is reported as "companion could not be run", a flaky failure unrelated to the app. The external plan review flagged this explicitly and the diff does not address it (no retry on address-in-use, no bind-port-0 discovery).
- Suggestion: Retry `startCompanion` once or twice when the health probe fails with an exit code that indicates a bind error, or have the server print the chosen port when given `--port 0` and read it from the log.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: medium
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/checks-lifecycle.ts:24-40 (`helper`)
- Finding: `spawnSync(..., timeout: 60_000)` assumes `companion.py start` daemonizes and exits. If the built helper runs the companion in the foreground (a legitimate reading of the brief), every lifecycle check blocks for 60 s per invocation and then fails with `exit null` — B01–B05 plus B27 burn ~5 minutes and fail for a harness reason. This is acknowledged in the answer key's calibration note, but there is no code to distinguish "helper hung" from "helper runs the server": the timeout produces `status: null` with no diagnostic distinguishing it.
- Suggestion: On a null status with no output, record evidence saying "helper did not return within 60 s (may run the companion in the foreground)" so the operator can tell a harness mismatch from an app bug.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/checks-runs.ts (B17, `lint`)
- Finding: `ctx.synthetic.find((i) => i.url === url)` for the "clean item" passes `undefined` into `items` (serialized as `null`) if the seed run has no item for `45900003`; likewise `variant()` silently falls back to `{}`. The check would then report "a clean item passes with ok true" as a failure caused by the app, when the real cause is a harness/seed mismatch. Same pattern in `checks-runs.expiry` (`mk` base `{}` if the agile url is absent — the `old` computation excludes that url defensively, but `mk` does not).
- Suggestion: Guard the clean-item check: if `find` returns undefined, record `p.note("the synthetic run holds no item for <url>")` and skip, instead of posting `null`.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/tour-baseline.ts:38-41 (`phone-picker` recipe)
- Finding: If `openBoard(page, ...)` throws inside the recipe (server slow, board error), the 390 px page's browser context is never closed — `reach.page` is never assigned, so the `finally`-style close at the end of `tourBaseline` never sees it. The error is converted to a `no(...)` reach, so the run continues with a leaked context (and its `**/*` route) for the rest of the tour.
- Suggestion: Wrap the body of the recipe in try/catch and close the context in the catch before returning `no(...)`.

- Category: test | Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/tests/unit/baseline-fixture.spec.ts:76-99 (fake-server test) and integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/checks-fetch.ts (`linkedinFetch`)
- Finding: `linkedinFetch` retries a second file *shape* only when the answer is a 400 matching `/quer/i` — a backend that reports "no active queries" with a different wording (or 503/other status) is not retried, and B11 then fails on the harness's guess about the undocumented `linkedin-queries.json` format. The answer key flags this as a first-run unknown, but there is no way for the check itself to mark the result "inconclusive on format" rather than "app failed".
- Suggestion: When both shapes produce a 4xx that mentions queries, record the outcome with evidence prefixed "unverified: linkedin-queries.json format assumption" so the operator can distinguish a harness guess from a real defect.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: low
- File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/src/baseline/board-ui.ts (`openThread` / `findItem` misses)
- Finding: `findItem` returns `{}` on a miss; `openThread` then calls `pickPlatform(page, "")` (regex `^\s*\b`, matches the first tab) and `getByText("")`, which either throws or clicks an arbitrary row — the resulting item failure names neither the missing thread nor the cause. All callers are wrapped in `recordProbe` so it fails loudly, but the evidence is misleading.
- Suggestion: In `openThread`, bail out early when `str(item.platform) === ""`, e.g. throw `new Error("thread not found in items")` so the probe evidence names the problem.

## What is solid

Spec compliance is good: all five ACs map to real code (byte-identical copy pinned by a digest test, fixture selection with a loud refusal for typos, the checklist/answer key with a per-item evaluator pinned from both TypeScript and Python tests, the approval stamped into the copy only and verified to preserve the digest, `<300`-line modules). The fake-service replay, the Probe pattern, the stub-backend pass/fail unit tests, and the "one recipe per screen" Python pin are genuinely behavior-validating. The shared-module changes (`checkSkillTriggers` phrase param, `Checklist.describe`, `variantFor` throwing for baseline) are additive and backward compatible; the old fixtures are covered by the selection unit test.

Overall: ship-with-fixes — the approach and coverage are sound; fix the port race retry, the leaked tour context, and the misleading not-found evidence paths before the first operator run.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
